newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Airlines sees return to profit in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Indian Airlines sees return to profit in 1997/98.

text.p: State-owned Indian Airlines, the nation's largest domestic carrier, expects to cut net losses in half this fiscal year and post a profit next year, Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim said on Friday.
"The net losses in 1996/97 will be 545 million rupees against 1.88 billion net losses in 1994/95," C.M. Ibrahim told a news conference. The 1996/97 fiscal year started on April 1.
The company posted a net loss of 1.1 billion rupees in 1995/96.
Ibrahim said the airline would come out of the red in 1997/98. "Next year we will go into net profit," he said.
Indian Airlines is seeking a technical collaboration for its existing jet engine overhaul complex, he said.

"We are going for a technical collaboration and after that a joint venture," Ibrahim said, adding that the airline had approached 11 engine-making firms and leading overhaul agencies in India and abroad for possible joint ventures.

Four companies have been shortlisted out of a total of eight firms, the minister said, citing Pratt and Whitney of the United States, Britain's Rolls Royce Plc, France's Sochata and India's Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd.
The airline is evaluating the proposals and will soon take a decision, the minister said.
